title: Free from Riches: The Path from Anxiety to Peace
subtitle: What Jesus said 2,000 years ago is exactly what you need to hear today

key_verse.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

cards.title: Jesus Did Not Speak from a Palace
cards.subtitle: His audience had real debts, just like you today
cards.content:
Before we enter into the words of Jesus, we need to see who He said them to. Because these words were not spoken at a theology conference. They were spoken on a hillside, out in the open, before people who knew anxiety firsthand.

🌍 GALILEE IN THE FIRST CENTURY:

The listeners of Jesus were farmers, fishermen, craftsmen, and small traders under brutal economic pressure:

• They paid tribute to the Roman Empire (up to 25% of their harvest)
• They paid the Temple tax in Jerusalem
• They lived with harvests that could be lost to drought or plague
• Their lands could be seized if they could not pay
• Many worked all day without knowing if they would eat tomorrow

This was not philosophy. It was survival.

💬 THEN JESUS SAID THIS:

'Take no thought for your life...'

He did not say it from a place of comfort. He said it looking at people who had real reasons to be anxious. And precisely because of that, what He said next was not a rebuke — it was a liberation.

🔄 TODAY IS THE SAME:

The names change: bills, debt, unemployment, economic crisis, uncertainty. But the pressure you feel in your chest when you do not know how you will make ends meet — that is exactly what they felt.

And the Jesus who spoke to them speaks to you today.
cards.revelation_key: Jesus did not design this message for people with perfect lives. He designed it for people like you, who have real reasons to be anxious and who need a real way out.

cards.title: Māmônā: The Word That Changed Everything
cards.subtitle: It is not just money. It is what you say 'Amen' to when you are afraid
cards.content:
'No man can serve two masters... Ye cannot serve God and mammon.' (Matthew 6:24)

📜 THE ORIGINAL WORD:

In the original text, Jesus used the Aramaic word **Māmônā** (מָמוֹנָא) — a word that translators in multiple versions and languages chose not to render, keeping it exactly as He pronounced it. That decision confirms the depth of its meaning and the magnitude of the message He wanted to convey.

In this study we will call it **'Riches'**, but its meaning goes far beyond money.

🔍 THE THREE DIMENSIONS OF Māmônā (Riches):

1. THE 'AMEN' OF THINGS (Trust)
The Aramaic root of Māmônā is 'mn — the same root from which the word 'Amen' comes.

Amen means: 'it is firm', 'it is trustworthy', 'I lean on this'.
Māmônā means: 'that which one trusts to feel secure'.

That is why Riches are not just banknotes. It is anything material to which you say 'Amen' when you are afraid of the future. It could be:
• Money and property
• A stable job
• A savings account
• Status or social connections
• Control over your own life

2. A RIVAL LORD (The Spiritual Entity)
Jesus does something revolutionary: He places Riches on the same level as God. He does not say 'you cannot use money and serve God.' He says 'you cannot serve two masters.' Money, when it becomes your source of security, ceases to be a tool and becomes a master.

Money 'speaks' to you. It gives you orders. It demands sacrifices: your time, your family, your ethics, your health. If you have ever said 'I have no choice' when in reality you did — but the price was financial — in that moment, Riches were your master.

3. ACCUMULATION AS A SHIELD (The Illusion of Security)
Riches represent the entire system of accumulation that promises to protect you from tomorrow. 'If I have enough, I will be safe.' That promise is the oldest in the world — and the most false.

⚡ THE QUESTION THAT CHANGES EVERYTHING:

What do you say Amen to when you are afraid?
What would you need to have or achieve to finally feel secure?

What you just answered in your heart — those are your Riches.
cards.revelation_key: Riches are not what you have in the bank. They are what your heart consults when fear arrives. Identifying what occupies that place is the first step toward freedom.

cards.title: The Treasure: The Magnet of the Heart
cards.subtitle: Your heart does not choose where to go. It follows the treasure automatically
cards.content:
Jesus begins His argument in verse 19, not verse 24. To understand the trap, you need to see how He builds it step by step.

📖 MATTHEW 6:19-21:
'Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven... For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.'

🧲 THE LAW OF THE MAGNET:

Verse 21 is not a moral observation. It is a physical description of how the human soul works.

It does not say: 'Put your heart where your treasure is' (as an instruction).
It says: 'Where your treasure is, THERE WILL your heart be' (as a law).

The heart follows the treasure as iron follows a magnet. It is not a conscious decision. It is automatic.

This explains something many people do not understand about anxiety:

You cannot simply 'decide' to stop being anxious.
You cannot force peace through determination.
Anxiety will remain as long as your treasure is on unstable ground.

When your security rests in something corruptible — your job, money, human relationships — your heart lives in permanent alertness because it knows, at some deep level, that treasure can be lost.

🪦 'MOTH AND RUST':

In the original Greek, Jesus uses two words His listeners understood perfectly:
• Moth (ses) — destroys linen and woolen garments (wealth stored in fabric)
• Rust (brosis) — literally 'that which eats', including mold and plagues that destroy stored grain

It was a direct image: everything you accumulate with so much effort carries within itself the seed of its own destruction.

✨ THE SOLUTION IS NOT 'TRY HARDER':

Jesus does not say 'try not to be attached.' He says 'change your treasure.' The solution to anxiety is not mental discipline — it is changing the magnet. When your trust rests in God (a treasure that cannot rust, corrupt, or be stolen), the heart finds rest.

💡 REMEMBER: Riches (Māmônā) = that which you trust to feel secure. Not just money — anything you consult first when fear arrives.

greek_words.meaning: To accumulate, to treasure up — to store for future security
greek_words.revelation: The word implies compulsive accumulation for the purpose of protection. Jesus does not forbid having things; He points to the act of accumulating as a shield against vulnerability — that is what enslaves.

cards.revelation_key: You cannot force peace. You can only change the magnet. When God becomes your real treasure, your heart rests because it knows that treasure cannot be lost.

cards.title: The Haplous Eye: How Riches Distort Your Vision
cards.subtitle: Anxiety does not only exhaust you — it makes you see people wrongly
cards.content:
After speaking about the treasure, Jesus does something unexpected. He does not move directly to money. He speaks about the eyes. Why?

📖 MATTHEW 6:22-23:
'The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single (haplous), thy whole body shall be full of light. But if thine eye be evil (poneros), thy whole body shall be full of darkness.'

🔍 THE KEY IS IN THE GREEK:

In our culture we read 'good eye' as 'spiritual focus.' But in the everyday Greek of the first century, these words had a very specific economic meaning:

👁️✅ HAPLOUS (good eye) = 'Simple, undivided, generous'
In the Greek of that era, 'haplous' described the person who gives without calculating, who keeps no double ledger in the heart, who can look at another and see them as a person — not as a threat or a resource.

👁️❌ PONEROS (evil eye) = 'Divided, stingy, greedy'
'Poneros' was the eye of the one who calculates, distrusts, compares. In the Hebrew Old Testament, 'evil eye' was a direct synonym for stinginess and greed.

💔 WHAT RICHES (Māmônā — that which you trust instead of God) DO TO YOUR VISION:

When Riches are your master, your eye becomes poneros (divided, calculating, greedy):
• You see people and calculate what they can give you or take from you
• You watch the news and only process what could affect your finances
• You see the needs of others but your first response is 'I cannot help, I am in need too'
• You look at the future and see only threats
• You even look at God with suspicion: 'Will He actually provide for me?'

That is darkness. It is not conscious wickedness — it is the natural result of an eye divided between two masters.

✨ WHEN THE EYE IS HEALED:

The haplous eye (generous, single-focused) fills the whole body with light. The person with a healthy eye:
• Can see others without calculating
• Can give without fear because they trust the Provider
• Can face the future without the burden of control
• Sees God as Father, not as a judge of their finances

The healing of the eye is the healing of one's complete perception of reality.

greek_words.revelation: The same root as 'haplotes' which Paul uses in 2 Corinthians 8:2 to describe the extreme generosity of the Macedonians in the midst of their own poverty. The healthy eye and generosity are the same thing seen from different angles.

greek_words.meaning: Evil, divided, stingy, generating weariness and pain
greek_words.revelation: The root 'ponos' means exhausting labor, pain. The divided eye does not only see poorly — it exhausts. Chronic anxiety has this dimension: the constant effort to control everything ends up destroying the one who attempts it.

cards.revelation_key: Anxiety does not only rob you of peace — it robs you of the ability to see people as they truly are. When God heals your vision, you can once again see with generosity.

cards.title: The Two Masters: The Diagnosis That Liberates
cards.subtitle: Your chronic anxiety is not weakness — it is the symptom of having two masters
cards.content:
We arrive at the climax of the argument. After speaking of the treasure (what you love), and the eye (how you see), Jesus comes to the will: whom you obey.

📖 MATTHEW 6:24:
'No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.'

🔑 THE WORD 'SERVE' IN THE GREEK:

Jesus does not say 'you cannot USE two masters.' He says 'you cannot SERVE' (douleuein — to be enslaved to). In the ancient world, a slave (doulos) was not an employee with two part-time jobs. He was absolute property. It was physically impossible to belong to two owners with opposing interests.

Jesus is saying: you are enslaved to something. The question is not whether you have a master — but who it is.

⚡ THE LIBERATING DIAGNOSIS:

This changes everything. Chronic anxiety is not:
✗ A flaw in your personality
✗ A lack of faith
✗ A weakness of character
✗ Something you must control with more willpower

It is the structural symptom of having two masters. When you try to control your security AND trust God at the same time, your soul lives in permanent tension. Two completely incompatible value systems fighting for first place.

💔 'HATE' AND 'LOVE' IN THE SEMITIC CONTEXT (the culture and thought of the ancient Middle Eastern peoples, including Hebrews and Arameans):

In Hebrew thought, 'love' and 'hate' are not primarily emotions — they are terms of covenant priority:

• Love = to choose, prioritize, be faithful to, put first
• Hate = to defer, put in second place, not choose

Jesus is not saying you will have feelings of hatred toward God. He is saying it is structurally impossible for two absolute priorities to occupy first place at the same time.

When a crisis arises, your heart will respond to one of the two. If Riches (Māmônā) are your true master, you run toward money, control, your own solution. If God is your master, your foundation and the owner of your life, you run toward Him.

🗝️ THE ACT OF LIBERATION:

Recognizing this is not condemnation — it is liberation. Jesus said it 2,000 years ago because it was true then and it is true today: when God does not occupy first place, something else occupies it in His stead. There is nothing wrong with you — there is a master who has governed you without your conscious choosing.

Today you can make the decision to replace it.

greek_words.meaning: To be enslaved to, to belong completely to
greek_words.revelation: Paul uses the same word in Romans 6:18: 'ye became the servants of righteousness.' Slavery to God is not oppression — it is the only slavery that produces real freedom.
Riches (Māmônā) receive the same title as God: Kyrios. By using this word, Jesus tells us that money is not neutral. When your security depends on it, it already holds the rank of lord in your life.

cards.revelation_key: Your anxiety is not your enemy — it is the honest signal that your heart is divided between two masters. And that signal is merciful: it is telling you exactly where the problem is and what the solution is.

cards.title: Merimna: The Mind Torn to Pieces
cards.subtitle: Jesus knew exactly what anxiety feels like from the inside
cards.content:
Immediately after speaking of the two masters, Jesus says: 'Therefore, take no thought.' The word He uses for 'thought' or 'anxiety' is one of the most descriptive in all the New Testament.

📖 MATTHEW 6:25-34:
'Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life... Is not the life more than meat? Behold the fowls of the air... Consider the lilies of the field... Are ye not much better than they?'

🧠 MERIMNA — THE WORD THAT DESCRIBES EVERYTHING:

The Greek word is 'merimnaō' (μεριμνάω), from the verb 'merizō' (to divide, to split) and 'nous' (mind).

Merimna = the mind torn to pieces.

It is not merely worry. It is the experience of having the mind literally fragmented across multiple simultaneous fronts of crisis:
• Work and money
• The future and the children
• Health and security
• What was and what might be

Do you recognize that feeling? The mind that cannot rest. The thoughts that arrive at 3am. The inability to be fully present because part of you is always calculating, anticipating, protecting itself.

That is merimna — the mind torn to pieces. And Jesus knew it by name.

🦅 THE ARGUMENT OF JESUS (A FORTIORI):

Jesus uses a classic rabbinical argument: from the lesser to the greater.

'Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?'

This is not naivety. It is a precise theological statement:

If the God who sustains all of creation — every bird, every lily, every blade of grass — is the same God who knows you by name and calls you His child, then there is a fundamental contradiction in living as though He does not exist or does not care.

💔 THE PHRASE THAT SUMS IT ALL UP (v.27):
'Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?'

Anxiety cannot change anything. It does not produce the results it promises. It only consumes.

✨ WHAT JESUS DID NOT SAY:

Jesus did not say 'do not work.' He did not say 'ignore your problems.' He did not say 'everything will automatically be fine.'

He said: 'But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.'

The promise is real. But it comes after a radical reorientation: the Kingdom first.

greek_words.revelation: Paul uses the same word in Philippians 4:6: 'Be careful for nothing' (merimnaō). And he writes it from prison. Freedom from merimna does not depend on the circumstances changing first — it depends on whose mind you belong to.

scripture_connections.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.

cards.revelation_key: Anxiety is not your enemy — it is the signal that your mind is divided. Jesus does not ask you to ignore your situation. He asks you to change whom you consult first when the situation arrives.

cards.title: Oligopistos: Jesus Does Not Abandon Those of Little Faith
cards.subtitle: Four times Jesus reached out His hand. Today the Spirit does the same from within
cards.content:
Here is the grace at the heart of this study. Jesus calls His disciples 'oligopistoi' — men of little faith. But He never abandons them for it.

🔍 OLIGOPISTOS — WHAT IT REALLY MEANS:

The Greek word oligopistos (ὀλιγόπιστος) comes from:
• Oligos = little, small, limited
• Pistis = faith, trust

It is not 'man without faith.' It is 'man of small faith.' There is an enormous difference.

Jesus does not say this as an insult — He says it as a diagnosis. Like a physician who identifies an illness not to condemn the patient, but to treat them.

📊 THE FOUR RESCUES OF JESUS FOR THE OLIGOPISTOI:

1️⃣ MATERIAL ANXIETY (Matthew 6:30-32)
Situation: People afraid of their economic future
Diagnosis: 'O ye of little faith'
Jesus' response: 'Your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things'
He does not rebuke them and leave. He reassures them: the Father knows them.

2️⃣ FEAR OF DEATH (Matthew 8:23-26)
Situation: Storm at sea, the disciples terrified
Diagnosis: 'Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?'
Jesus' response: He arose and rebuked the winds and the sea
He does not wait for them to have more faith before acting. He acts so that their faith may grow.

3️⃣ SINKING IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAY (Matthew 14:28-31)
Situation: Peter walks on water, sees the wind, begins to sink
Diagnosis: 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?'
Jesus' response: 'And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him'
'Immediately.' Without delay. Without conditions. The hand extended before the sermon.

4️⃣ SPIRITUAL POOR MEMORY (Matthew 16:8-9)
Situation: The disciples worry about having no bread, minutes after witnessing the miracle of the loaves
Diagnosis: 'O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves?'
Jesus' response: He patiently reminds them of what the previous miracles accomplished
The oligopistos needs to remember. Jesus teaches with patience.

🕊️ THE TRANSITION: FROM THE JESUS WHO RESCUES FROM WITHOUT TO THE SPIRIT WHO STRENGTHENS FROM WITHIN:

Jesus knew He would not be physically with us forever. That is why He promised the Paraclete — the one who comes to walk alongside.

'But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost... shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.' (John 14:26)
→ When the mind is torn between a thousand anxieties, the Spirit brings the exact promise you need.

'The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.' (Romans 8:26)
→ When you do not even know how to ask for help, the Spirit connects your heart to the Father.

'Ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance.' (Ephesians 1:13-14)
→ The Spirit is the living guarantee that you are a child of God — the security that Riches (Māmônā — that which you trust to feel secure) promise but can never give.

🔥 THE DIFFERENCE:

Jesus calmed the external storm.
The Spirit calms the internal storm.

Jesus reached out His hand from outside the water.
The Spirit sustains you from within the storm.

scripture_connections.text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
Ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.

cards.revelation_key: The same Jesus who stretched out His hand to Peter in the sea today extends His Spirit to your mind so you do not sink in anxiety. He does not wait for you to have perfect faith before helping you. He acts so that your faith may grow.

cards.title: The Paradoxical Secret of the Kingdom
cards.subtitle: When you stop looking only at your own need and see the need of another, God takes care of you
cards.content:
There is a principle that appears repeatedly in the Bible and that runs completely against the logic of anxiety.

Anxiety says: 'Focus on yourself. Protect yourself. Accumulate. Control. Solve your own problems first.'

The Kingdom says something radically different.

📖 MATTHEW 6:33:
'But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.'

The 'kingdom of God' is not only a vertical relationship. It is acting in favor of others as God acts in favor of you.

🧩 THREE EXAMPLES THAT DEMONSTRATE IT:

1️⃣ JOB — THE MAN WHO PRAYED FOR THOSE WHO FAILED HIM (Job 42:10)
'And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends.'

Job was in the worst of his crisis — he had lost everything. His friends had wounded him with their words. And God asked him to pray for them.

He did not pray for himself. He did not negotiate with God. He interceded for those who had failed him.
And at that exact moment, God restored everything.

2️⃣ THE WIDOW OF ZAREPHATH — HER LAST HOPE (1 Kings 17:10-16)
In the midst of an unending famine, this woman was not at her last grain of flour in a physical sense alone — she was at something deeper: she had made the decision to give up. Her own words say it: 'that we may eat it, and die.' She was no longer fighting. She had already let go of hope.

And precisely there, in that total surrender, Elijah asks her to give first. Before giving to herself. Before giving to her son.

She obeys. And God enters exactly where human hope ended.
Result: 'The barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail.'

It was not the last food. It was the last hope. And that makes the miracle all the more powerful.

3️⃣ PAUL — WRITES 'BE CAREFUL FOR NOTHING' FROM PRISON (Philippians 4:6-7)
Paul writes the most powerful words about peace not from comfort, but from a prison cell. He writes them to console others while he himself is imprisoned.

He lives the principle while he preaches it. And his peace is so real it confounds his Roman guards.

⚡ THE SPIRITUAL LOGIC:

When you focus only on your own need, Riches (Māmônā — that which you trust instead of God) have all the power over you. You are solely responsible for your own security, and that burden crushes.

When you release that logic and act in favor of the other who has your same problem — you pray for them, you help them, you listen to them — you are doing something Riches cannot understand:

You are demonstrating with your body that God is your Lord, not fear.

And God responds to that demonstration of faith with His provision.

🌱 THE CONCRETE CHALLENGE:

Who do you know today who has your same struggle?
Who is going through what weighs on you?

Before you pray for yourself today, pray for that person.
Before you seek a solution to your problem, ask someone how you can help with theirs.

That is not naivety. It is the most revolutionary act you can take against anxiety.

scripture_connections.text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.

There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty. The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

cards.revelation_key: The greatest act of faith against anxiety is not to pray more for yourself. It is to release your need long enough to see the need of another. In that act, God demonstrates that He is real.

cards.title: The Examination of the Heart: To Whom Do You Say Amen?
cards.subtitle: The moment to move from knowledge to real freedom
cards.content:
You have reached the most important moment of this study. This is not a moment for more information — it is a moment for decision.

Everything you have read points to one place: the state of your heart today.

discovery_questions.question: What do you say 'Amen' to when you are afraid? What would you need to have, achieve, or control to finally feel secure? (Whatever that is, those are your Riches — your current Māmônā.)

Is your eye haplous (generous, single-focused) or poneros (divided, calculating) right now? Can you see the people around you with generosity, or has anxiety made you see them as threats, competition, or instruments?
When a financial or security crisis arrives, what is your first real reaction? Do you run toward God or toward a plan B? That response tells you who your real master is in that moment.
Who do you know today who has your same struggle or a similar one? Could you pray for that person before finishing this study, before asking for yourself?
Like the disciples in Matthew 16, do you have 'poor spiritual memory'? When was the last time God provided, cared for you, or intervened in your life? Write it down. Remember it today.

prayer.title: Prayer of Liberation and Surrender
prayer.content:
Heavenly Father, we come before You with an honest heart, not with perfect words.

We acknowledge today that we have had two masters. That many times we have said 'Amen' to money, to control, to material security before saying it to You. That our heart has been calculating and divided, looking at others with distrust — when we want to be focused on You alone, free to give without fear.

Thank You because You do not call us 'men without faith.' You call us men of little faith — as we read in Your Word. And that means faith is there, though small, though afraid. And that You do not let go of the hand of the one who is sinking.

Today we acknowledge that this mind that cannot rest, that tears itself between a thousand worries at the same time, is the signal that we have tried to serve two masters. And we declare today, before You, that we choose one Lord alone. That You are the owner of our life. That to You we say Amen.

Deliver us from Riches. Not from having things — but from things having us. Not from working — but from working as slaves to fear. Heal our vision so we may once again see people with generosity. Restore our sight so that the future does not come with uncertainty, but drives us toward You.

And give us grace to practice the Kingdom principle: to release our own need long enough to see the need of another. Help us to pray today for someone who is struggling with the same thing we are. To give when we are afraid to give. To trust when the numbers do not add up.

May Your Holy Spirit be today what You said He would be: the one who reminds us of Your promises when fear speaks, the one who intercedes when we have no words, the one who seals us as children when Riches tell us we are slaves.

We seek Your Kingdom first. We trust that everything else comes after.

In the name of Jesus, who came poor so that we might know true riches, Amen.

action_steps.title: The Daily Question of the Heart
action_steps.description: Every morning, before checking your phone or the news, ask yourself: 'To whom am I going to say Amen today?' It is a decision made consciously each day, not once and for all.

action_steps.title: The Riches Inventory
action_steps.description: This week, write honestly: what are you most afraid of losing? What would be hardest to let go of? Not to condemn yourself — but to identify exactly where Riches have influence in your heart and bring it specifically before God.

action_steps.title: Practice the Paradoxical Principle
action_steps.description: Identify someone who is going through a struggle similar to yours. This week, pray specifically for that person before praying for your own situation. Observe what happens in your heart when you do.

action_steps.title: Build Your Spiritual Memory
action_steps.description: Write in a visible place three specific moments when God provided, cared for you, or intervened in your life. When the mind tears itself between a thousand worries (and it will), read that list. The one of little faith needs to remember. Give your faith the help of memory.

action_steps.title: An Act of the Generous Eye
action_steps.description: Do an act of generosity this week that costs you something — time, money, effort. Not to earn points with God, but to train your eye to see beyond your own need. Generosity is the muscle that weakens Riches. It is the simple, undivided eye in action.

cards.identity_statement: You are not a slave to anxiety. You are not a prisoner of your circumstances. You are a child of the Father who looked at the lilies and the birds and said: 'You are worth much more.' This mind that cannot rest does not have the last word over your life. He does.

themes: Little faith that Jesus does not abandon
The paradoxical principle of the Kingdom
The Holy Spirit as inner peace
Generosity as the antidote to Riches
